question: A 9-year-old boy diagnosed as uncomplicated pulmonary tuberculosis. He is put on isoniazid, rifampin, and ethambutol at home after initial treatment given at hospital. Which is accurate statement for this scenario?

options.opa: His 3-year-old sibling should receive INH prophylaxis
options.opb: A baseline test of auditory function test is essential before drug treatment is initiated
options.opc: Polyahralgia is a potential adverse effect of the drugs the boy is taking
options.opd: His mother, who takes care of him, does not need INH prophylaxis

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "3-year-old sibling" -> "close contact with TB patient" -> "high risk of TB infection" -> "INH prophylaxis recommended" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Isoniazid" -> "peripheral neuropathy" -> "not auditory function" -> "auditory test not essential" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Mother" -> "close contact with TB patient" -> "risk of TB infection" -> "INH prophylaxis recommended" -> 85%
analysis: In the context of tuberculosis management, especially in pediatric cases, it is crucial to consider the risk of transmission to close contacts. Isoniazid (INH) prophylaxis is recommended for young children who are close contacts of a TB patient, as they are at high risk of developing the disease. This aligns with standard TB prevention guidelines, making option opa the most accurate statement. Option opb is incorrect because auditory function tests are not essential for the drugs mentioned; isoniazid is more associated with peripheral neuropathy. Option opc is less accurate because polyarthralgia is not a common side effect of the drugs listed. Option opd is incorrect because the mother, as a close contact, should also be considered for prophylaxis. Therefore, the most accurate and consensus-supported option is that the 3-year-old sibling should receive INH prophylaxis.
